stat 230 - lec 12 conditonal prob

def: P(A|B) = P(A n B) / P(B) provided P(B) > 0
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$$

indep events: A and B are indep iff $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$
- mutualy exclusive is NOT the same as indep!!
- if P(A)>0 and P(B)>0, mut excl events cant be indep

bayes rule
$$P(B \mid A) = \frac{P(A \mid B)P(B)}{P(A)}$$

example: test for disease, sens 0.95, spec 0.9, prevalance 0.01 -> P(D|+) approx 0.088

sim in R (prof showed this):
```
set.seed(230)
x <- rbinom(10000, 1, 0.01)
mean(x)
```
